draft.title: The Ottawa Charter
card: The Ottawa Charter is a framework for health promotion released by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1986. It sets out five action areas that governments, services and communities can use.

Building healthy public policy: laws and rules that make healthy choices easier, such as tobacco taxes or helmet laws. Creating supportive environments: safe, healthy places to live, learn and work, such as shaded playgrounds or well-lit bike paths.

Strengthening community action: local groups set their own health goals and work together to reach them. Developing personal skills: teaching people knowledge and skills, such as how to cook or read food labels.
Reorienting health services: shifting health services from only treating illness to also preventing it, such as a clinic that adds screening tests.
draft.remember: Five action areas: public policy, supportive environments, community action, personal skills and reorienting health services.

a.q: A local council makes a rule that bans smoking in all outdoor dining areas. Which Ottawa Charter action area does this show?
a.why: A ban is a rule made by a council, so it is healthy public policy. It is not developing personal skills, because it changes the rules and does not teach people anything new.
a.clue: Think about who made the rule.

b.q: A hospital in Bendigo moves some nurses from its wards to run free blood pressure checks at local shopping centres. Which action area is this?
b.why: The hospital is changing how its own staff work, moving from caring for sick patients toward finding problems early. That is reorienting health services. It is not creating supportive environments, because the shopping centre itself is not made any safer or healthier.
b.clue: Whose work has changed, and toward what?

Reorienting health services: shifting health services from only treating illness to also preventing it, such as a clinic that adds screening tests.
